questions.question: Who among the following was given the charge of looking after the imperial household during the Mughal administration?
questions.solution:
• Mir Saman was given the charge of looking after the imperial household during the Mughal administration.
  • Mir Bahri (mir-i-bahr) was responsible for the maintenance of river and seaports.
  • Mir Bakshi headed the military department, nobility, and information and intelligence agencies.
  • Mir-e-aatish was the head of the ordinance department.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding foreign travelers to India:
1. Jean-Baptiste Tavernier, a French jeweler, traveled to India several times during the Mughal period, especially in the reign of Shah Jahan.
2. Antonio Monserrate was a Spanish missionary who came to India during the reign of Shah Jahan.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: Jean-Baptiste Tavernier, a French jeweler, visited India six times during Shah Jahan's reign.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: Antonio Monserrate was a Spanish missionary who came during Akbar's reign, not Shah Jahan's.

questions.question: Who built the Pathar Ki Masjid in Patna, Bihar?
questions.solution: • Parwez Shah (son of Mughal Emperor Jahangir) built 'Pathar Ki Masjid' on the banks of the River Ganga in Patna, Bihar in 1621.

questions.question: On 12 August ______ the Mughal emperor appointed the East India Company as the Diwan of Bengal.
questions.solution: • On 12 August 1765, the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II appointed the East India Company as the Diwan of Bengal.

questions.question: ______ in Gujarat was the emporium of western trade during the Mughal Period.
questions.solution:
• Surat in Gujarat was the emporium of western trade during the Mughal Period.
  • It grew famous for all types of textiles, particularly cotton textiles.

questions.question: The Mughal court chronicles are written in
questions.solution:
• Mughal court chronicles such as the Akbar Nama were written in Persian.
  • Famous books during Mughal reign:
    • Humayun Nama - Gulbadan Begum
    • Tuzuk-e-Babari - Babur
    • Akbar Nama - Abul Fazl
    • Tarikh-e-Akbari - Abul Fazl
    • Tahakik-e-Hind - Al-Biruni
    • Laila Majnu - Amir Khusrau
    • Shahnamah - Firdousi

questions.question: With reference to the Land Revenue System of Mughal Empire, the term ______ was the amount assessed.
questions.solution:
• The term 'Jama' was the amount assessed in the land revenue system of the Mughal Empire.
  • The arrangements for collection consisted of two stages: first assessment (Jama) and then actual collection (Hasil).
  • Banjar was the worst kind of land left out of cultivation for five years or more.

questions.question: Which Mughal prince translated the Upanishads into Persian in 1657?
questions.solution:
• Dara Shikoh, the eldest son and heir-apparent of Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, translated the Upanishads into Persian in 1657.
  • He completed the translation of fifty Upanishads from Sanskrit to Persian so they could be studied by Muslim scholars.

questions.question: Who was the Mughal Emperor at the time of Battle of Plassey?
questions.solution: • Aziz-ud-din Alamgir II (Reign: 1754-1759) was the Mughal Emperor at the time of the Battle of Plassey (1757).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the battles of Babur:
Statement 1: The Battle of Khanwa (1527) was fought between Babur and Rana Sanga.
Statement 2: The Second Battle of Panipat (1527) was fought between Babur and Hemu.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is incorrect, Statement 2 is correct
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: The Battle of Khanwa in 1527 was fought between Babur and Rana Sanga. Babur emerged victorious, strengthening his control over northern India.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The Second Battle of Panipat occurred in 1556 between Hemu and Akbar, not involving Babur.

questions.question: The real name of Babur, the founder of Mughal dynasty in India was:
questions.solution:
• The real name of Babur was Zahiruddin Muhammad.
  • Real names of some other Mughal emperors:
    • Humayun - Nasir al-Din Muhammad
    • Akbar - Jalal-ud-din Muhammad Akbar
    • Jahangir - Muhammad Salim
    • Aurangzeb - Muhi-ud-din Muhammad

questions.question: Medini Rai of Chanderi, Hasan Khan of Mewat and Mahmud Lodi joined Rana Sanga with their forces to fight against which of the following Mughal rulers?
questions.solution:
• Medini Rai, Hasan Khan of Mewat, and Mahmud Lodi joined Rana Sanga to fight against Babur.
  • Babur was a descendant of Genghis Khan and Timur, and founded the Mughal Empire in northern India.

questions.question: The battle of Khanwa was fought between the forces of Babur and the Rajput forces led by:
questions.solution: • The Battle of Khanwa was fought between Babur and the Rajput forces led by Rana Sanga.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the use of Gunpowder in North India:
Statement 1: Babur made the use of gunpowder common in North India to defeat his enemies.
Statement 2: Ibrahim Lodi introduced gunpowder in the Deccan region for the first time.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: Babur was the first to use gunpowder effectively in North India, especially in the First Battle of Panipat (1526) against Ibrahim Lodi.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: Gunpowder was not introduced by Ibrahim Lodi in the Deccan.

questions.question: Who was the eldest of four sons of Babur?
questions.solution:
• Humayun was the eldest of Babur's four sons.
  • He was the second ruler of the Mughal empire.
  • The Afghan soldier Sher Shah Suri defeated him at Chausa (1539) and Kannauj (1540).
  • Humayun was the first person to develop a citadel in Delhi named 'Din Panah'.

questions.question: The first battle of Panipat took place between Babur and
questions.solution:
• The First Battle of Panipat was fought in 1526 between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi.
  • Second Battle of Panipat (1556): Hemu Vikramaditya and Akbar.
  • Third Battle of Panipat (1761): Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali.

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor built the Moti Masjid in Agra?
questions.solution:
• Shah Jahan built the Moti Masjid (Pearl Mosque) in Agra.
  • It is located within the Agra Fort complex.

questions.question: The battle of Chausa was fought between Humayun and
questions.solution:
• The Battle of Chausa was fought in 1539 between Humayun and Sher Shah Suri.
  • Humayun was defeated, which led to the rise of the Suri dynasty.

questions.question: The 'Din-i-Ilahi' was a religious path propounded by
questions.solution:
• Akbar propounded 'Din-i-Ilahi' (Divine Faith) in 1582.
  • It aimed to merge the best elements of various religions.
  • The first initiated disciples included Birbal, Prince Salim (Jahangir), and Abul Fazl.

questions.question: Which of the following is the burial place of Humayun?
questions.solution:
• Humayun's Tomb in Delhi is the burial place of Humayun.
  • It was built by his widow Bega Begum.
  • The architect was Mirak Mirza Ghiyath.

questions.question: Mirza Kamran was the brother of which of the following Mughal emperors?
questions.solution:
• Mirza Kamran was the brother of Humayun and son of Babur and Gulrukh Begum.
  • He came to India in 1538.

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor did Maharana Pratap face in the Battle of Haldighati?
questions.solution:
• The Battle of Haldighati (1576) was fought between Maharana Pratap of Mewar and the Mughal forces under Man Singh I of Amer, representing Emperor Akbar.
  • It was triggered by Maharana Pratap's refusal to accept Mughal suzerainty.

questions.question: Akbar's first expedition towards Deccan was sent to Ahmednagar under the leadership of Prince Murad and
questions.solution:
• Akbar's first expedition towards the Deccan was sent to Ahmednagar under the leadership of Prince Murad and Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan.
  • Akbar was the third Mughal emperor, ruling from 1556 to 1605.

questions.question:
Match the following Navratnas of Akbar with their respective roles:
1. Raja Todar Mal → (a) Defence Minister
2. Abul Fazl → (b) Prime Minister and chief advisor
3. Abdul Rahim → (c) Revenue Minister
4. Tansen → (d) Culture Minister and Singer
questions.solution:
• The correct matching is:
    • Raja Todar Mal - Revenue Minister
    • Abul Fazl - Prime Minister and chief advisor
    • Abdul Rahim - Defence Minister
    • Tansen - Culture Minister and Singer
  • Other Navratnas: Faizi (Education Minister), Birbal (Foreign Minister), Raja Man Singh (Chief of Staff), Mullah Do Piyaza (Home Minister), Fakir Aziao-Din (Religious Minister).

questions.question: After the death of Humayun, the 13-year-old Akbar was coronated in 1556 at Kalanaur in
questions.solution:
• Akbar was crowned at Kalanaur in Punjab on February 14, 1556.
  • He came to power under the guidance of his guardian Bairam Khan.
  • He later defeated Hemu in the Second Battle of Panipat, securing control over Delhi.
